cultural.vision_reason: This is a backstrap loom with a partially woven red-and-black wool textile with bird motifs, a type of weaving equipment used by Otomi and related Mexican highland peoples; it is household/craft equipment, not a musical instrument, so the claimed category "instruments" is wrong but the object itself fits the culture.

physical.title: loom
physical.summary: Backstrap loom for double-weaving; made of wood; with a section of red and black wool textile with bird motifs already woven. Basic construction: 1) dowel at top wrapped with warp threads; 2) reed twined through warp threads; 3) reed twined through warp threads; 4) flat piece of wood with tapered ends; 5) reed twined through warp threads; 6) reed twined through warp threads; 7) reed twined through warp threads; 8) flat piece of wood with tapered ends; 9) small flat piece of wood with tapered ends; 10) reed bobbin with red wool wrapped around it; 11) reed bobbin with black wool wrapped around it; 12) extra dowel to roll up finished textile; 13) dowel with warp threads wrapped around it; 14) weaver's strap (mecapal in Spanish) plaited from vegetable fibre for strapping around weaver's waist.
